nodes.label: Taycan portfolio specification
nodes.description: Portfolio in a Porsche Taycan; this README specifies a future browser experience.

nodes.label: Approved concept; application unscaffolded
nodes.description: Visual concept approved; all implementation milestones pending, with no working commands, production assets or deployed website.

nodes.label: Developer and founder portfolio
nodes.description: Communicate Rajdeep Pandey's work; driving and games are optional extensions.

nodes.label: First playable browser milestone
nodes.description: Enter Taycan, use desktop, open Fermeon, return, start car, drive a finite circuit and return to preserved desktop state.

nodes.label: Showroom and cabin entry
nodes.description: Useful initial HTML, separate car loading, scroll-controlled door/camera entry and Skip to Portfolio.

nodes.label: Linux-inspired desktop shell
nodes.description: Top bar, dock, launchers and useful initial Work/About window; reachable focusable windows with close and maximise/restore.

nodes.label: HTML dashboard integration
nodes.description: Real DOM surface aligned through CSS transforms or Drei Html; non-interactive during entry, readable after camera settles.

nodes.label: Direct portfolio and project routes
nodes.description: /portfolio and /projects/[slug] provide accessible, shareable content without mandatory 3D.

nodes.label: Structured portfolio content
nodes.description: One structured content source powers direct routes and desktop applications.

nodes.label: Experience mode transitions
nodes.description: Showroom, Entering, Desktop, Starting, Driving, DrivePaused and Arcade with explicit failure, return and resume transitions.

nodes.label: Exclusive input ownership
nodes.description: Exactly one of desktop, embedded app, driving or arcade owns keyboard input; focus changes clear held keys.

nodes.label: Explicit start/pause/dispose lifecycles
nodes.description: Driving and arcade must explicitly manage physics, audio, timers and game loops; visibility alone is insufficient.

nodes.label: Start Drive readiness gate
nodes.description: Click unlocks audio and loads driving; remain stationary until assets are ready and countdown completes.

nodes.label: Portfolio return and explicit resume
nodes.description: Pause simulation and sound, preserve desktop state, then restore driving only through explicit Resume Drive.

nodes.label: Next.js, React and TypeScript layer
nodes.description: Application routes, readable case studies, metadata, desktop and fallback views.

nodes.label: Three.js through React Three Fiber
nodes.description: Render car, studio, cabin, lighting, cameras and track.

nodes.label: Selected Drei utilities
nodes.description: Model loading, environment helpers and HTML-to-scene alignment where appropriate.

nodes.label: Single scroll/timeline system
nodes.description: GSAP is the initial candidate for door/camera choreography and transition progress.

nodes.label: Rapier through React Three Rapier
nodes.description: Collision and contact queries for an arcade vehicle controller.

nodes.label: Small typed shared state store
nodes.description: Zustand is a candidate for experience mode, selected app, preferences and driving session.

nodes.label: Algorithm and browser verification
nodes.description: Unit tests for meaningful state/input/track behavior, Playwright browser journeys, visual inspection and device profiling; update milestones only after demonstrated exits.

nodes.label: Client-side subsystem boundaries
nodes.description: Content-route imports must not initialise browser rendering, physics, games or audio; select compatible versions and one lockfile at scaffolding.

nodes.label: Fixed-step simulation and UI separation
nodes.description: Keep frame data outside React UI state; use fixed steps, optional render interpolation and clamped accumulated time after suspension.

nodes.label: Application registry
nodes.description: Separate configuration from presentation; suggested fields cover IDs, enabled status, icons, case-study and launch/embed URLs, allowed origins and initial sizes.

nodes.label: About, Work, Experience, Résumé and Contact
nodes.description: Useful initial portfolio window and familiar desktop controls; approved résumé/profile content and contact links define application scope.

nodes.label: Fermeon live application candidate
nodes.description: Primary AI-memory product candidate. A 13 September 2026 landing check returned 200 with no observed X-Frame-Options or CSP; useful embedded flow remains untested.

nodes.label: TryDonna framing-blocked candidate
nodes.description: Case study and external launch planned. A 13 September 2026 response included X-Frame-Options: DENY; embedding requires a scoped policy change.

nodes.label: ClawIN live application candidate
nodes.description: Case study and live candidate. A 13 September 2026 landing check returned 200 with no observed framing headers; browser interactions still require testing.

nodes.label: Meetly optional disabled launcher
nodes.description: Disabled by default; preserve the agreed URL. The 13 September 2026 landing check returned 404; inclusion must not block launch.

nodes.label: Lazy live iframe integration
nodes.description: Load only an opened product; retain local introduction, external launch, scoped capabilities, expected-origin communication and message validation.

nodes.label: Scoped embedding and frame policies
nodes.description: Controlled demo routes permit the eventual portfolio origin through CSP frame-ancestors and resolve conflicting framing headers; portfolio frame sources are configured separately.

nodes.label: Parent-owned Return/Close controls
nodes.description: Keep surrounding controls accessible even when focus is in a cross-origin iframe; Escape remains supplementary.

nodes.label: Real iframe flow tests and recovery
nodes.description: Test useful tasks, authentication, cookies, redirects and popups; supply cancellation and recovery despite limited cross-origin failure detection.

nodes.label: Concept Taycan source model
nodes.description: Mikhail Hamanovich's model is the existing concept source; embedded metadata identifies CC BY 4.0, requiring preserved attribution and modification records.

nodes.label: Historical concept asset findings
nodes.description: Approximately 3,007,135 triangles and 93,743,444 raw geometry bytes; custom door work and further cabin/screen refinement needed. Findings are from the concept workspace.

nodes.label: Blender and glTF Transform workflow
nodes.description: Establish scale, moving parts, pivots, repaired materials and simplified collision geometry; export and validate articulated GLB assets and document measurements.

nodes.label: Moving car parts and screen anchors
nodes.description: Preserve door hinges, wheels, steering wheel, display and camera anchors, and collision proxy through optimisation.

nodes.label: Per-asset provenance manifest
nodes.description: Track ID, creator, source/licence URLs, attribution, acquisition, checksum, modifications, runtime files, sizes and quality tier; provide notices.

nodes.label: Prepared runtime assets and source storage
nodes.description: Keep runtime models/textures/audio/icons in public assets; raw projects and render caches outside normal checkout, with large-source storage and future CDN decisions pending.

nodes.label: Candidate lighting, road and scenery assets
nodes.description: Unselected alternative Taycan; candidate Poly Haven HDRI/props and ambientCG road material; optional Kenney prototype geometry and approved product logos.

nodes.label: Arcade vehicle controller
nodes.description: Tune predictable motion, fixed steps, collision response, visual wheel/cluster agreement and recovery; choose Rapier controller or custom integration after prototype.

nodes.label: Finite handling test track
nodes.description: Small circuit precedes endless generation and is used to tune acceleration, braking, steering, stopping and recovery.

nodes.label: Keyboard and touch driving controls
nodes.description: W/Up accelerate, S/Down brake, A/D or arrows steer, R recover, Escape pause only when driving owns input; visible recovery and touch controls required.

nodes.label: Bounded endless road system
nodes.description: Queue of connected segments with entry/exit poses, curvature, elevation, width, mesh references and collision data; one initial landscape.

nodes.label: Deterministic constrained segments
nodes.description: Seed generation; build ahead and constrain joins, slopes, curvature and intersections to remain drivable; place checkpoints relative to centreline.

nodes.label: Mesh, scenery and collider recycling
nodes.description: Recycle distant sections and reuse mesh/material/prop pools, including colliders as well as visible geometry.

nodes.label: Coordinated world-coordinate rebasing
nodes.description: Periodically rebase physics bodies, track references and camera anchors while preserving logical distance.

nodes.label: Position-independent logical distance
nodes.description: Keep accumulated distance independent of rebased coordinates; seeded routes can support later time trials or ghosts.

nodes.label: Versioned local driving records
nodes.description: Store local distance and best runs with graceful handling of unavailable storage; remote score services are unnecessary initially.

nodes.label: Covered studio-to-track transition
nodes.description: Preserve car and cabin camera; load the track, update cluster, blend lighting and conceal scenery changes through an exit/tunnel; failure returns to parked desktop.

nodes.label: Shared Web Audio context and mixer
nodes.description: Resume from Start Drive, smooth pitch and volume, crossfade layers, control output and persist mute/volume preferences.

nodes.label: Responsive electric-car sound layers
nodes.description: Power-on, motor linked to throttle/speed, road/wind, braking, door and restrained interface effects.

nodes.label: Background and mode audio suspension
nodes.description: Pause/suspend on backgrounding, focus loss, game/desktop transitions and errors; explicit driving resume and no duplicate or abandoned loops.

nodes.label: Audio provenance and synthesized first pass
nodes.description: Factory sound is a design reference requiring a suitable source/licence; original synthesized layers may precede licensed recordings.

nodes.label: Optional Doom Arcade application
nodes.description: A concept WebAssembly experiment rendered the engine, but a maintained runtime, appropriate release data and input/audio/lifecycle integration remain to be selected.

nodes.label: Doom runtime and release-content decision
nodes.description: Select engine and lawful game-content distribution explicitly; Freedoom is a distinct alternative, not a silent original-Doom substitution.

nodes.label: HTML-first staged loading
nodes.description: Render profile/project HTML first; request 3D, detailed cabin, driving and arcade progressively, with genuine progress or recoverable loading states.

nodes.label: Unmeasured initial performance targets
nodes.description: Approximate desktop 60 fps, mobile 30 fps, initial 3D transfer 8–12 MB or lower, bounded memory/counts and idle-loop avoidance; validate on named hardware.

nodes.label: Accessible and resilient visitor paths
nodes.description: Skip/direct routes, reduced motion, visible focus, labels, contrast, keyboard/touch navigation, WebGL/model/site fallbacks, predictable scrolling and no sound autoplay.

nodes.label: Maximised and small-screen flat views
nodes.description: Stable typography, scrolling and pointer mapping; conventional flat application layout on small screens or without 3D.

nodes.label: Pending implementation phases 0–6
nodes.description: Scaffold; car/screen proof; portfolio desktop; finite drive; endless environment; full apps/arcade; release preparation. Every checklist remains pending.

nodes.label: Unresolved implementation and release choices
nodes.description: Final car quality, screen geometry, theme, controller integration, hosting/origin/embed routes, Doom distribution/mobile support, measured budgets and optional Meetly.

nodes.label: Useful content must precede immersion
nodes.description: The core purpose is communicating work; optional car entry, driving and games must not obstruct portfolio access.

nodes.label: Cross-origin websites require a real HTML surface
nodes.description: A cross-origin website cannot simply be drawn into a Three.js canvas texture, motivating real HTML alignment.

nodes.label: Parent cannot depend on iframe keystrokes
nodes.description: Cross-origin iframe focus prevents reliable parent receipt of Escape or other keys, so surrounding controls must remain accessible.

nodes.label: Visibility does not stop active subsystems
nodes.description: Hiding a scene alone leaves physics, audio, timers and game loops running; explicit lifecycle management is necessary.

nodes.label: Post-download simplification misses loading cost
nodes.description: Simplifying only after downloading the original roughly 94 MB geometry cannot solve the first-load transfer cost.

nodes.label: Prove integrated interactions before expansion
nodes.description: First establish that portfolio content, screen, car and controls work together; endless environment and complete arcade follow.

nodes.label: CORS does not grant iframe framing permission
nodes.description: Iframe restrictions require relevant application changes and a chosen portfolio origin; this specification changes no live configuration.

nodes.label: Rebasing limits long-drive precision loss
nodes.description: Long sessions need coordinated coordinate rebasing without losing logical distance.

nodes.label: Engine licence does not grant game-data rights
nodes.description: Open-source engine rights do not imply permission to redistribute original Doom assets; Freedoom remains a different game.

nodes.label: Per-frame React rerenders are avoidable
nodes.description: High-frequency vehicle transforms should not rerender the React component tree every frame.

nodes.label: Iframe load is not proof of a usable app
nodes.description: Framing failures and cross-origin errors cannot all be reliably detected by the parent, requiring useful flow testing and visible recovery.

nodes.label: Named-device profiling and sustained-drive evidence
nodes.description: Choose reference devices, browsers and network profiles before enforcing budgets; record measurements and inspect viewport, zoom, orientation, focus and touch.

hyperedges.label: First playable proves content, dashboard, car and controls together
Exactly one keyboard owner among desktop, embedded app, driving and arcade
